data.title: Arista Revenue Jumps 58.5% as AI Demand Lifts Its 2027 Outlook
data.description:
Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) reported its fastest annual revenue growth since going public on November 3 and outlined another year of strong expansion for 2027. The results connect rising demand for AI networking with a larger near-term sales base, while also showing the inventory commitments needed to support it.

Revenue for the quarter ended September 30 was $3.66 billion, up 58.5% from a year earlier and 20.5% from the second quarter, according to the company’s earnings release. That exceeded Arista’s prior $3.3 billion guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%, compared with 48.6% a year earlier; the GAAP margin was 44.9%.

Fourth-quarter revenue guidance is $3.9 billion to $4.0 billion, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.26 to $1.30 a share. The company expects a non-GAAP operating margin between 48% and 49%. Those targets point to higher sales than the reported quarter, without assuming that the latest adjusted margin will continue unchanged.

On the earnings call transcribed by Investing.com, management lifted its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $13.3 billion and gave an initial 2027 growth range of 38% to 40%, or approximately $18.5 billion at the midpoint. These are company projections, not analyst consensus estimates.

Management also reported inventory of $3.2 billion, up from $2.5 billion in the previous quarter, and purchase commitments of $11.4 billion, up from $9.7 billion. The call linked that investment to meeting demand for new products and AI deployments. It also cautioned that inventory timing can affect cash flow before customer deployments.

The 2027 growth range is lower than the latest quarter’s 58.5% annual increase, although it applies to a larger revenue base and a full year rather than one quarter. Arista’s outlook therefore describes continued rapid expansion, with supply planning and conversion of inventory into customer shipments remaining part of the execution task.

data.title: Democrats Win Congress, Shifting Markets’ Focus to Policy Constraints
data.description:
Democrats won control of the U.S. House and Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, according to the Associated Press. The outcome changes the policy setting for markets heading into the next Congress, with President Donald Trump facing opposition control of both chambers.

Reuters reported early on November 4 that U.S. stock-index futures recovered from initial declines as investors assessed the result. Its report highlighted uncertainty around artificial intelligence oversight, cryptocurrency regulation and taxes. Those are areas of potential policy change, rather than measures enacted by the election itself.

The next Congress takes office in January. Until then, the election outcome is a change in expected political control, not an immediate transfer of committee powers or a new set of corporate rules. That timing matters when separating a market response to the result from the effects of legislation that has yet to be written or passed.

Divided government also leaves a substantial constraint on new laws. As the National Archives explains, the president can veto legislation, and overriding that veto requires a two-thirds majority in both chambers. Winning congressional majorities is therefore not the same as securing the votes needed to enact a disputed policy over presidential opposition.

Reuters described concerns about greater scrutiny of the AI industry and its infrastructure buildout. That creates a different question from whether spending on data centers is currently growing: oversight can affect future conditions even when corporate order books remain strong. The election result alone does not establish the content, timing or financial impact of any eventual restriction.

For companies, the practical sequence now runs from committee priorities and proposals to negotiated legislation or other concrete action. The result changes who can set part of that agenda. It does not yet resolve tax rates, technology rules or the earnings effects for individual businesses, and it supplies no automatic direction for stocks.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: DuPont Raises Profit Outlook After Healthcare and Water Demand Drives Q3 Growth
data.description:
DuPont (NYSE: DD) raised its 2026 profit outlook on November 3 after growth in healthcare, water and industrial markets supported stronger third-quarter earnings. The materials company also announced plans for an additional $250 million of share repurchases in the fourth quarter.

Net sales for the quarter ended September 30 rose 4% to $1.868 billion. Organic sales increased 5%, partially offset by currency effects, according to DuPont's results announcement. GAAP earnings from continuing operations were $1.24 a share, while adjusted earnings reached $2.09.

DuPont now expects full-year adjusted EPS of $7.47–$7.52 and operating EBITDA of about $1.785 billion. These are non-GAAP measures. Operating EBITDA measures earnings before specified costs, and should not be treated as equivalent to GAAP net income.

Reuters reported that the prior annual adjusted EPS range was $7.17–$7.32. DuPont's fourth-quarter forecast of $1.90–$1.95 a share also exceeded the $1.87 analyst average compiled by LSEG.

Healthcare & Water Technologies sales rose to $865 million, while Diversified Industrials sales exceeded $1 billion. DuPont said higher segment earnings, lower interest expense and a lower tax rate and share count helped adjusted EPS. The earnings improvement therefore reflects financing and capital-allocation effects as well as operating growth.

Continuing operations generated $410 million of operating cash flow. Transaction-adjusted free cash flow was $341 million, compared with $346 million a year earlier. That comparison adds useful context to the higher earnings: stronger per-share profit did not translate into growth in every cash-flow measure.

data.title: Yum’s Pizza Hut Sale Boosts Reported Profit as Taco Bell Sales Slip
data.description:
Yum! Brands (NYSE: YUM) reported a sharp increase in third-quarter GAAP profit on November 3, but most of the headline jump reflected the sale of Pizza Hut. Beneath that gain, earnings excluding special items edged lower and Taco Bell's same-store sales declined.

For the quarter ended September 30, GAAP earnings were $5.92 a share, compared with $1.41 a year earlier. EPS excluding special items was $1.56, down from $1.58, according to Yum's earnings release. Reported operating profit included an approximately $1.7 billion pre-tax gain from the Pizza Hut divestitures.

The company completed the mainland China sale on August 7 and the sale of the brand outside mainland China on September 1. Current-period results include Pizza Hut only up to those dates, while the prior-year comparison includes the business throughout. Excluding Pizza Hut from both periods, Core Operating Profit grew 1%.

KFC's same-store sales increased 1% and unit count grew 7%. Taco Bell's same-store sales fell 4%, while its unit count rose 3%. That contrast separates growth from opening restaurants from demand at established locations.

StreetInsider reported that the $1.56 earnings figure exceeded its cited $1.53 analyst estimate, while revenue of about $2.05 billion fell short of its $2.10 billion forecast. Those comparisons use the estimates reported by that source.

The sale gain changes reported profit, while the brand-level sales figures describe the operations Yum retains. Treating the two separately makes clear why the larger GAAP earnings number does not, by itself, establish stronger underlying restaurant performance.

data.title: U.S. Job Openings Reach 7.52 Million as Quits Rise in September
data.description:
U.S. job openings reached 7.523 million in September, up from a revised 7.190 million in August, according to the labor-market report released November 3. The higher vacancy count came alongside an increase in voluntary quits, offering a fuller picture than the openings figure alone.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics release described job openings as little changed over the month, with a vacancy rate of 4.5%. Its published tables show an increase of 333,000 positions. The agency's characterization and the numerical movement should be read together when assessing the strength of the signal.

The Associated Press reported that openings were the highest since May, with hiring rising and layoffs falling in the underlying estimates. BLS nevertheless characterized the monthly changes in both hires and layoffs as small.

Hires totaled approximately 5.4 million, while layoffs and discharges were about 1.6 million. Quits increased to roughly 3.4 million. Voluntary departures can provide information about workers' willingness or ability to leave a job, rather than measuring employers' decisions to cut positions.

These figures describe different stages of the labor market. Openings are positions available on the last business day of September; hires and separations count payroll movements throughout the month. A vacancy therefore should not be treated as a completed hire or an addition to net employment.

For stock-market readers, the report bears on the balance between labor demand, household income and wage costs. It offers evidence about September conditions, while leaving the direction of subsequent hiring—and any policy response—to later data.

data.title: Marvell’s $115 Billion Lumentum Deal Draws Analyst Downgrades
data.description:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) faced fresh analyst downgrades on November 3 after agreeing to acquire Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion. The debate is moving from the strategic appeal of optical connectivity to the price and timing of combining the businesses.

Investing.com reported that TD Cowen lowered Marvell to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $175 from $350. Bank of America moved to Neutral from Buy and reduced its target to $225 from $400. Their concerns included earnings dilution, the optical industry's cycle and a lengthy approval process.

The November 2 agreement gives Lumentum shareholders 4.500 Marvell shares for each share held. They would own approximately 33% of the combined company, with current Marvell investors holding about 67%. The companies expect closing in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

That fixed share exchange makes the ownership split a clearer guide to the transaction than a dollar value that changes with the stocks. The announced valuation is not a fixed cash payment to Lumentum investors.

Marvell says combining its connectivity and custom-silicon capabilities with Lumentum's lasers and optical components can support more integrated AI infrastructure. It projects more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost savings and an increase in non-GAAP earnings per share in the first year after closing.

TD Cowen's reported forecast instead anticipates mid-single-digit percentage earnings dilution in that first year. That is an analyst assessment, separate from management's projection. The disagreement puts demand assumptions, savings and the additional share count at the center of the financial case for the deal.

data.title: Eaton Raises Growth Outlook as Electrical Backlog Climbs 46%
data.description:
Eaton (NYSE: ETN) raised its 2026 organic growth outlook on November 3 after electrical-equipment demand drove a sharp increase in sales and orders. A 46% rise in electrical backlog gives the power-management company a larger pipeline of work to deliver.

Third-quarter revenue reached $8.9 billion, up 28% from a year earlier. Eaton's earnings release attributed 19 percentage points of growth to organic sales, eight to acquisitions and one to currency. Separating those contributions shows that expansion within existing operations supplied most of the increase.

Reported earnings were $2.77 a share, while adjusted earnings reached $3.68. The latter excludes acquisition and divestiture charges, intangible amortization and restructuring effects. Segment margins reached 25.3%, above the top of the company's guidance range.

Electrical Americas recorded 39% growth in its twelve-month rolling average of organic orders, while Electrical Global posted 51%. Combined electrical backlog grew 46% year over year. Backlog represents business still to be delivered, so its growth should not be treated as revenue already recognized.

Eaton now expects full-year organic sales growth of 13%–15% and adjusted earnings of $13.70–$13.80 a share. StockTitan's review of the results also highlighted fourth-quarter adjusted earnings guidance of $4.05–$4.15 and a projected segment margin of 25.4%–25.8%.

The results connect demand for power infrastructure with actual shipments and profitability, giving the story relevance beyond software and semiconductor earnings. Converting the larger order book into sales remains an execution task: capacity, delivery timing and costs determine how much of that demand ultimately becomes profit.

data.title: Pfizer Raises 2026 Outlook as Non-COVID Medicines Drive Growth
data.description:
Pfizer (NYSE: PFE) raised its full-year revenue and adjusted earnings forecasts on November 3 as growth outside its COVID-19 franchise helped offset declining pandemic-product sales. The upgrade offers a stronger outlook even though total third-quarter revenue was broadly unchanged.

The drugmaker now expects 2026 revenue of $62 billion–$64 billion, up from $60.5 billion–$62.5 billion. It lifted and narrowed adjusted diluted earnings guidance to $2.95–$3.05 a share from $2.80–$3.00, according to its earnings announcement. The revenue midpoint increased by $1.5 billion.

Quarterly revenue totaled $16.583 billion, compared with $16.654 billion a year earlier. Reported diluted earnings fell to $0.56 a share from $0.62, while adjusted earnings were unchanged at $0.87. These are different profit measures and should not be read interchangeably.

Excluding Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenue increased 7% operationally, a comparison that strips out foreign-exchange effects. Pfizer's defined group of launched and acquired products grew 32% on the same basis. That narrower product-group figure is not the growth rate for the whole company.

Reuters reported that adjusted earnings exceeded the $0.73 analyst estimate compiled by LSEG and revenue topped a $15.87 billion forecast. Its report identified demand for cancer medicines and Eliquis as drivers, while highlighting patent expirations as a challenge to longer-term revenue.

The updated outlook includes a $650 million acquired in-process research and development charge associated with Pfizer's Innovent collaboration, with an approximately $0.10-per-share adverse impact. Growth from newer medicines and higher development spending are arriving together; the raised forecast does not eliminate the cost of replenishing the product portfolio.
